rows.concrete_observation: Read entire501-line EntityMurmurHead and entire EntityMurmur, both renderers. Two actual EntityTypes register body/head, body.createHead constructs linked head and addFreshEntity. Server body.tick rebuilds missing linked head and stores UUID plus synced integer ID. Server head.getBody resolves UUID in current ServerLevel, client uses synced integer ID. Native head.hurt first rejects its own isInvulnerableTo (super OR IN_WALL). Otherwise it asks resolved body.hurt(source,0.5*damage); TRUE returns immediately, FALSE or missing body FALLS THROUGH super.hurt(source,full damage) on independent head. This is not an always-rejected shield-part nor unconditional parent forwarding: a source denied by BODY may still injure HEAD. Body class has no hurt/isInvulnerableTo override; native base/event policies can still refuse. Predicate not duplicated into head from body. Body reference is any Entity, no reciprocal UUID/type/alive/generation validation inside hurt. Server head.tick validates body only in other paths; missingbody after20ticks discard. When body is present, head hurt/death sounds return null even if local fallback health takes damage; body sound remains its own native hook. Client head.tick copies body hurtTime/deathTime when either>0. Renderer uses getOverlayCoords(head,...) also for neck segments, and body optional fake-head pass reads body overlay; so displayed hurt feedback can reflect parent timing while actual fallback changed separate head HP. Do not promote timer replay as another credit: existing VoidWorm already covers replay. Head target attack sound occurs before target.hurt and ignores hurt bool, also only a boundary contrast,0extra.
